reason: The cited evidence directly supports the formation of L12 precipitates via Al+Ti additions and their thermal stability, but it does not address the claimed retention of environmental resistance, radiation tolerance, or cryogenic toughness in the dual-phase state, leaving those key premises unsupported.
premises: FCC HEAs have low yield strength (~200 MPa as-cast) but excellent cryogenic ductility/toughness
Adding Al+Ti to an FCC HEA can form ordered L12 (γ′) precipitates
γ+γ′ HEA systems show thermal stability, coarsening resistance, and strength retention up to ~800°C
The γ′ phase has a stoichiometric composition (Ni,Co)3(Ti,Al) in Ni-Co-Fe-Cr-Al-Ti HEAs
Precipitation hardening by ordered precipitates can overcome the low yield strength of FCC HEAs
